title: Diagramming & graphs — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: One of the most complete planes in the library: 25 notations — flowchart, DRAKON, BPMN, UML, Petri nets, fault trees, ER, Gantt, fishbone, molecules, choropleths — all rendered by one engine, over a native deterministic layout engine and a NetworkX-tier graph-algorithm suite (Dijkstra, A*, SCC, betweenness, PageRank, Louvain, max-flow). Math and molecule diagrams are genuinely constraint-solved via autodiff, not merely placed. And a fact correction the code forced: the old `dot.exe` dependency is demoted to an optional viewer — diagram layout is now engine-native. Guarded by ~1,790 assertions.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Diagramming spans two peer worlds at once — Mermaid/D2/Graphviz for pictures, NetworkX for the graph maths — and this plane reaches into both.

lanes.engine: 25 notations (DN0–DN24), ~21 Ring faces — flowchart, org chart, workflow/statechart, BPMN, UML, electric, DRAKON, math, storyboard, molecule, Gantt, ER, Petri, fault tree, family tree, timeline, fishbone, network, floor plan, seating, choropleth — all as profiles over one renderer (`stzDiagram`), not separate tools.
lanes.owed: A catalogue that rivals or exceeds Mermaid's, and the "one renderer, notations as data profiles" architecture is distinctive. The domain list is closed by design.

lanes.engine: `graph_layout.zig` (GG1): barycentre crossing-reduction (best-keeping — "never makes a picture worse", total-order tiebreak), seeded Fruchterman-Reingold `force`, coordinate placement and alignment relaxation — bit-identical within and across processes, proven by a determinism guard.
lanes.owed: A native, deterministic layout engine — determinism as a guarantee (Graphviz is not bit-stable) is a real distinction. Edge-routing quality for hard graphs is the frontier (lane 10).

lanes.engine: `graph.zig` (CSR) ships a broad suite: BFS/DFS, Dijkstra, A*, SCC, articulation points, bridges, bipartite check, topological sort, cycle detection, betweenness / closeness / PageRank / k-core / Louvain, diameter/radius/clustering, MST, and max-flow / min-cut / min-cost-max-flow — engine-implemented, not Ring loops.
lanes.owed: At NetworkX-core parity for traversal, shortest-path, centrality, components and flow — and compiled, so faster than NetworkX's Python. The long tail (generators, isomorphism) is lane 11.

lanes.engine: Math (DN7) and molecule (DN11) diagrams are genuinely solved, not placed — the layout is a system of constraints minimized by the engine's autodiff solver (`StzEngineGrad*`), with interactive re-solve: `DragTo` / `Pin` re-minimize around a held shape.
lanes.owed: No mainstream diagramming tool solves layout as an optimization problem with a real gradient. Distinctive; the reach is extending it to more notations (lane note in Tier C).

lanes.engine: One renderer, three outputs: `ToSVG()` (vector, no device), `ToPNG()` (GPU-backed), and an ASCII visualizer; 24 node shapes; plus DOT-source export. "Needs no GPU and no graphviz" for the SVG floor.
lanes.owed: No PDF / PostScript export (Graphviz's publication formats), and PNG needs a GPU device. SVG + ASCII + DOT cover most needs; the print formats do not ship.

lanes.engine: A command-based editing session: `Edit`, `Undo`/`Redo`, `EditLog`, `PickAt(x,y)`, `RewireAnchor` — undoable commands, not raw mutation, with illegal edits refused at the gesture by the notation's own rules.
lanes.owed: A programmable, governed edit API — but not a visual WYSIWYG node editor (explicitly out of scope), and live pan/zoom belongs to the GUI plane (lane 12).

lanes.engine: `stzGraphRule` and `stzOrgRule` feed the one CI gate (`stzRuleReport`, unified finding shape), with concrete rules like no-orphan-position and separation-of-duties (approver ≠ executor) — a diagram that can check its own structure.
lanes.owed: A distinctive graph-governance layer, shared with the security/code-rule domains — but the shipped rule catalogue is small. Room for a real structure-linting library on top.

lanes.engine: `stzGraph` exports DOT, JSON, GraphML and YAML (`Dot()`, `RenditionAs`), emitting standard graph-interchange text for other tools.
lanes.owed: Good export breadth; import parity is thinner, and GEXF / Pajel / adjacency-matrix round-trips aren't all present. Export-strong, import-lighter.

lanes.engine: Dedicated label discipline: notation-in-a-label (DN10), labels centred on cap-height not the em-box (DN12), curve clearance (DN13), and solver-placed labels (`SolveLabelsAfter`) on the constrained diagrams.
lanes.owed: Careful, typographically-correct label placement most tools approximate — a genuine strength narrowed only by being tied to the notations that use it, not a general label-layout service.

lanes.engine: For the diagram notations, hierarchical and force layout are engine-native. For arbitrary large-graph visualization, `stzGraph` emits DOT and offers an optional `dot.exe` viewer (`Display()`).
lanes.owed: The native engine hasn't met the "dot kill criterion": spline edge routing and nested-cluster layout, where dot still wins. General graph visualization therefore still leans on the external viewer — the one runtime dependency left.

lanes.engine: The analysis core is deep, but the surrounding utilities NetworkX bundles are thin: no standard graph generators (Erdős-Rényi, Barabási-Albert, Watts-Strogatz) and no isomorphism / graph-edit-distance surfaced.
lanes.owed: Random-graph generators for testing/benchmarking and (sub)graph isomorphism / matching — the utility long tail that rounds out a graph-analysis library beyond the algorithm core.

lanes.engine: Diagrams emit interactive SVG (ids / classes / titles) and support programmatic re-layout (`Relayout`, `DragTo` re-solves), so a host can wire hover and selection.
lanes.owed: No built-in live pan / zoom / brush — that is the GUI plane's reactive layer over these hooks, not the diagram module's own. Interaction stops at the SVG contract.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first retires the last external dependency; the second adds reach and print/utility breadth; the third is editing and analysis depth.

tiers.title: Tier A — retire the last dependency

items.title: Meet the dot kill criterion
items.text: Native spline edge routing and nested-cluster layout for general graphs, so arbitrary `stzGraph` visualization no longer needs the `dot.exe` viewer at all. It is the single external runtime dependency left, and the plan already scopes its retirement.

items.title: Live interactivity via the GUI plane
items.text: Pan / zoom / brush on the interactive-SVG hooks the diagrams already emit — wiring the reactive GUI layer to the diagram contract turns strong static pictures into explorable ones.

items.title: Graph generators & isomorphism
items.text: Erdős-Rényi / Barabási-Albert / Watts-Strogatz generators and (sub)graph isomorphism / edit distance — the NetworkX utilities that make the strong algorithm core a complete analysis library.

items.title: PDF / PostScript export
items.text: An SVG→PDF/PS path for publication, the one output family Graphviz has and this renderer does not. Small over the existing vector renderer, high value for print/paper figures.

items.title: Import parity
items.text: Round-trip the interchange formats it exports (GraphML / GEXF / adjacency), so graphs authored elsewhere load cleanly, not just export out.

items.title: A visual node editor
items.text: WYSIWYG editing over the command-based edit session (currently out of scope). It would make the governed edit API a draw.io-class tool while keeping the "illegal edits refused at the gesture" guarantee.

items.title: Extend constraint-solving to more notations
items.text: The autodiff solver that lays out math and molecule diagrams could place other notations where a constraint model beats a heuristic — turning "solved" from two notations into a general option.

items.title: A real structure-governance catalogue
items.text: Grow `stzGraphRule` / `stzOrgRule` from a few rules into a broad architecture / process-linting set feeding the one CI gate — the governance the plane's rule seam is built for.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main` (the session's working branch was stale), and one memory claim was corrected against code: force/hierarchical layout no longer shells out to `dot.exe` for the diagram plane — it runs in `graph_layout.zig`; dot survives only as an optional viewer and as the not-yet-met kill criterion for general graph layout. The guards are heavy: ~1,790 `chk`/`chkeq` assertions in the adversarial gate discharging 76 plan items, a determinism guard proving bit-identical layout, and 158 algorithm test files. No `#ERR`/`#SKIP`.

Softanza diagramming is a genuine two-world standout — a 25-notation renderer with Mermaid-plus breadth and a NetworkX-tier graph engine under it, with constraint-solved layout no competitor offers — and its remaining distance is the polish of general large-graph layout (edge splines, clusters), the utility long tail (generators, isomorphism, PDF), and live interaction, which is the GUI plane's to add.
